Vice-President Urges Global Research Partnerships at Dr NTR University Ruby Jubilee

Call for International Academic Collaborations

Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan has called upon Dr NTR University of Health Sciences (NTRUHS) in Vijayawada to establish partnerships with leading global research institutions. Speaking as the chief guest at the university's Ruby Jubilee celebrations on Monday, the Vice-President noted that international collaborations would provide medical students with access to advanced facilities and facilitate the exchange of scientific knowledge to address major health challenges.

During his address, Radhakrishnan emphasized the importance of fostering a robust research culture among healthcare professionals. He expressed optimism that future researchers from the institution could achieve significant milestones, including finding breakthrough treatments for critical illnesses such as cancer.

Growth in National Medical Education Infrastructure

Highlighting broader developments in India's medical education sector, Radhakrishnan pointed to official capacity figures. He stated that the number of medical colleges nationwide has grown from 387 prior to 2014 to 846 projected for 2026. Additionally, undergraduate MBBS seats have increased by 172 percent—rising from approximately 51,000 to 1.40 lakh—while postgraduate medical seats have expanded to nearly 86,000.

The Vice-President also addressed the integration of modern technology, noting the expanding roles of artificial intelligence and telemedicine in diagnostics and treatment access. However, he cautioned that technological advancements must remain balanced with compassion, urging physicians to maintain a strong human touch in patient care.

Public Health and Regional History

Addressing contemporary social issues during the event, Radhakrishnan appealed to the medical community to take a proactive stance against substance abuse and contribute to community awareness efforts aimed at building a drug-free society.

He also paid tribute to the university's origins, recalling the contributions of former chief minister N.T. Rama Rao, who founded NTRUHS in 1986. The commemorative event was attended by several notable figures, including Andhra Pradesh Governor S. Abdul Nazeer, National Medical Commission official Dr. M.K. Ramesh, Information and Public Relations Minister K. Parthasarathy, Vijayawada MP Kesineni Sivanath, and NTRUHS Vice-Chancellor Dr. P. Chandrasekhar.
